result.title: Human-Inspired Asymmetric Collaboration for Dual-Student Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
result.summary: Dual-student learning enriches predictive diversity in SSMIS by introducing a strongly augmented view alongside a weakly augmented view. Insufficient strong augmentation may homogenize the students, whereas excessive augmentation can corrupt anatomical evidence and destabilize collaboration. This challenge echoes feedback-regulated human instruction, where learners receive differentiated tasks and the task difficulty is continually adjusted according to their evolving responses. Inspired by these, we propose Human-Inspired Asymmetric Collaboration (HAC), a closed-loop dual-student framework that maintains weak--strong learning through adaptive difficulty calibration and geometry preservation. Specifically, Reinforcement-guided Difficulty Calibration (RDC) formulates strong-augmentation control as a window-level reinforcement learning process, using augmentation history, realized perturbations, and training responses to dynamically adjust the augmentation magnitude, operation number, and magnitude range. Meanwhile, the Gramian Geometry Preservation Constraint (G2PC) preserves the early-stage three-branch geometry through global volume and pairwise area constraints, preventing shared supervision from homogenizing the two students. Comprehensive evaluations across LA, Pancreas, and BraTS-2019 validate both the segmentation effectiveness and capability-aware difficulty calibration of HAC.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向半监督医学图像分割，提出 HAC 双学生非对称协作框架：以窗口级强化学习动态校准强增强难度，并用 Gramian 几何保持约束（全局体积与成对面积）防止共享监督使两个学生同质化。在 LA、Pancreas、BraTS-2019 上验证分割效果与难度校准能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但 G2PC 这类显式保持表示几何、抵抗监督导致的同质化（坍缩）的约束，以及用训练反馈闭环调节难度的机制，可能为核查 latent 状态表征坍缩与动态计算分配提供借鉴线索，需人工确认可迁移性。
